capToLow.prompt: Which is the lowercase letter of the capital letter {up}?
hints: Think of the capital and lowercase letters as pairs.
Be careful with letters that look alike, such as b, d, p and q.

lowToCap.prompt: Which is the capital letter of the lowercase letter {low}?
hints: Think of the capital and lowercase letters as pairs.
Imagine writing the lowercase letter big and tall.

pairPick.prompt: Choose the pair in which the capital and lowercase letters match.
hints: In each pair, the first letter is a capital and the second is lowercase.
Check one by one whether the lowercase letter is the same letter as the capital.
pairPick.expl: {ans} is a matching pair of a capital and a lowercase letter.

sameStart.prompt: Which word begins with the same sound as “{word}”?
hints: Say the first sound of “{word}” out loud.
Look for a word that starts with the same sound. The first letters may be different.
sameStart.expl: “{word}” and “{ans}” both begin with the sound {sound}.

storyFirst.prompt:
Read the passage and choose what happened first.

"{text}"
hints: Look for words that show order, such as First, Then, Next and Finally.
What happens in the sentence with First comes first.
storyFirst.expl: “{ans}” comes after First in the passage, so it happened first.

storyLast.prompt:
Read the passage and choose what happened last.

"{text}"
hints: Look for words that show order, such as First, Then, Next and Finally.
What happens in the sentence with Finally comes last.
storyLast.expl: “{ans}” comes after Finally in the passage, so it happened last.

storyAfter.prompt:
Read the passage and choose what happened right after '{event}'.

"{text}"
hints: First find the sentence in the passage with “{event}”.
Then look at what happens in the very next sentence.

punct.prompt: Choose the sentence with correct capital letters and punctuation.
hints: Capitalise the first letter of a sentence, people's names, and I.
End the sentence with the mark that fits it (. ? !).

sumPick.prompt:
Choose the sentence that best summarises the passage.

"{text}"
hints: Find the main idea that the whole passage keeps coming back to.
A sentence about only one detail, or about something not in the passage, is not a good summary.
sumPick.expl: “{ans}” covers the main idea of the whole passage, so it is the best summary.

E3abc1.title: Capital and lowercase letters
E3abc1.concept: The alphabet has **capital letters** and **lowercase letters**. Many pairs look different, so learn them one pair at a time. Take special care with letters that look alike, such as b, d, p and q.

E3snd1.title: Sounds and spelling
E3snd1.concept: The first sound of a word is linked to its first letter. Find words that begin with the same sound to learn how sounds and spelling are related. Sometimes two letters, such as ph, make the f sound.

E6seq1.title: Finding the order of events
E6seq1.concept: Words that show order, such as **First**, **Then / Next**, **After that** and **Finally**, tell you the order in which things happened.
E6seq1.example: First, I wake up. Then I eat breakfast. Finally, I go to school.

E6pun1.title: Capital letters and punctuation
E6pun1.concept: A sentence starts with a **capital letter** and ends with the right **punctuation mark**: a period (.) for a statement, a question mark (?) for a question, and an exclamation mark (!) for surprise or strong feeling. People's names and the word I are always capitalised.
E6pun1.example: Is this your bag? Yes, it is.

M2sum1.title: Summarising a passage
M2sum1.concept: To summarise, find the **main idea** and shrink it to one or two sentences. A sentence about only one detail, one that adds something not in the passage, or one that is too broad is not a good summary.
M2sum1.example: Recycling saves resources and reduces trash.
